title: Knowing When to Fall Back After a Drive Fleet Changes
grain: One maximal consecutive run of equal binned SMART indicators for a pseudonymous drive
question: When monitoring signals disappear after a fleet change, is switching to an interpretable rule worth the lost warnings?
design: Keep the complete fleet's observation calendar. Train on earlier, disjoint serials and exclude one entire model. Evaluate fifteen daily alerts on unseen serials or the excluded model. Keep every observed candidate at allocation, then report unobservable follow-up separately; differentiate missing from zero. Compare a fixed pending-sector rule, a frozen empirical score and a fallback triggered by unavailable indicators or matured poor precision.
boundary: A recorded hardware failure is a proxy for replacement need. A late and an absent failure are distinguishable only while the drive remains observed. Alternative dispatch rules are replayed on logged outcomes.
redistribution: Backblaze permits sharing the data with attribution. The extract reports binned measurements and pseudonyms.
